input: p and q are integers satisfying 1 <= q <= p <=1000. They describe the square side and first east-wall interception height from receptor zero in the stated mirror-room geometry. Integers are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays, excluding holes, proxies, subclasses and accessors; strings are primitive rather than boxed. Standard built-ins are unmodified; no concurrent mutation or custom field access occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The first reached receptor number: zero at the southeast corner, one at the northeast corner, or two at the northwest corner, for a ray starting southwest toward the east wall at height q. It returns one when p=q.
mutation_aliasing: Only scalar local copies of p and q are halved; caller values and instance state are unchanged.
numeric: Remove common factors of two while both values are even. These exact halvings preserve positive integers, so no truncation or floating tolerance is involved. Once a value is odd, parity determines the first unfolded corner: even p gives 2, even q gives 0, otherwise 1. All values remain in [1,1000].
complexity: O(log(p+1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Only common powers of two are needed because odd common divisors cannot change the reduced parity. There is no iterative geometric ray simulation, floating trigonometry or lcm product.
